title: Update the logo
description: Resize the document to match the logo size. Add a text path layer.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 582ba51a - Resources: Update the logo
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/9880/diffs?diff_id=612301982&start_sha=7224bfbf1f106c18692669eaa15fa3c9f70411f9)

This used to render as the sharkfin on top of 'WIRESHARK' and decorated with an (R).
Now when looking at the rendering in gitlab, it looks like just the sharkfin with some smudges at the upper edge of the image. Is that supposed to be like this?

Confirmed. If I load the svg in Edge, there's something at the top that extends beyond the upper border.

![image](/uploads/415106f7b023e9282274f40f557b9793/image.png)

This isn't really an SVG file; it's an [Inkscape SVG](https://wiki.inkscape.org/wiki/Inkscape_SVG_vs._plain_SVG) file. According to that wiki page,

> Inkscape SVG should render identically with or without the Inkscape extensions

but that doesn't seem to be the case here. If I load the updated logo in Firefox I see the same thing as Gilbert's image, but If I load it in Inkscape it shows up just fine:

![inkscape](/uploads/5cd5aa941d8553beeb30b33ec3ead414/inkscape.png)

Additionally, if I export the file as a "Plain SVG" it renders fine in Firefox. I can add a plain version of the file if needed, but I'd vote for merging the file as is since it lets us use Inkscape's layers and other features.
Perhaps put "inkscape" in the name, so people aren't confused why it doesn't load properly eveywhere? "wslogo.inkscape.svg" ?
